Subject: Recap + next steps — Embeddings integration (vector dims, batching, normalization)

Hi Kyle / Sana —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discussion and recommended next steps so we can get an integration plan on the calendar: 

What we heard
- You currently use VendorX embeddings (768d) for semantic search across product docs and support tickets.
- You’re planning a migration to reduce costs and improve recall for short queries.
- Key constraints: 100k monthly active queries, median response target <200ms, and strict PII policies (S3 data residency).

Open technical questions
1) Target vector dimensionality: are you flexible to move to 1536d? We recommended 1536 for compatibility with our curated models + better accuracy on reranking. If you must stick to 768d for storage reasons, we can map/quantize.
2) Batching / throughput: please share peak QPS and average batch sizes for embedding calls (we discussed 1–2k qps peaks).
3) Normalization: do you normalize on your side currently (L2/float32 normalization), or rely on VendorX client?
4) Existing IDs/metadata: attach a sample of the CSV mapping (id, text, metadata) — see attachment placeholder.

What we propose
- Short technical workshop (30–45m) with Dev Patel to run a live SDK demo (Python + Node) showing auth, streaming, and a small migration test using a 1k-row sample.
- Migration plan options: direct re-embed (recommended) vs. mapped conversion (if you need to keep 768d).
- Baseline pick: 1536 dims + L2 normalization + mini-batches (128–512) on upload for cost/perf balance.

Next steps
- Kyle: send a 500–1k row sample CSV (id,text,metadata) and confirm peak QPS.
- We’ll schedule the workshop — availability windows below.

Availability (PST) for workshop: Wed 7/29 10:00–12:00, Thu 7/30 09:00–11:00, Fri 7/31 13:00–15:00.

Attached: acme_data_embed_schema.csv (sample mapping), redwood_embedding_guide.pdf (short doc on dims/normalization).

Kyle —

Quick technical notes from a serving perspective: 

- Normalization: Redwood's embeddings ingestion accepts either raw or already-normalized vectors. If you send raw vectors we'll normalize server-side (L2) before indexing so similarity is consistent. If you pre-normalize, we'll detect and skip normalization to avoid double-scaling — please flag in the upload metadata (upload.normalize=true/false).

- Dimensionality: 1536 is our recommended default for our curated models (higher accuracy and reranker tuning). If you must keep 768 for storage, we can: 1) continue using VendorX vectors for live queries + Redwood for new content; or 2) convert 768->1536 using a learned projection layer (adds complexity and slight accuracy variance).

- Batching: for large bulk uploads we recommend chunk sizes of 128–512 rows per request. Single-row requests are fine for low QPS. For your nightly job (~100k rows), use parallel workers with batches of 256 and backoff on 429s. This balances memory and throughput on our dedicated upload paths.

- Write timeouts: use the SDK client with retry/backoff (we'll share sample code in the workshop). For streaming ingestion, set socket timeout to 60s for large batches.

- Migration option: run a small A/B on a subset of queries (test index) and compare recall/latency. We can provide a reranker evaluation harness to measure quality differences between 768 and 1536 outputs.

I’ll put a short demo together for the workshop showing: Python SDK upload example (batching + normalize flag), server-side detection of dims, and a reranker comparison.

—Dev
